reuse.why: The tree already exports getScheduledAmount in shared/schedules.ts (null -> 0, number passthrough, range -> amount) used by the UI, but the diff ignores it and introduces a parallel getExpectedScheduleAmount.

duplication.why: It removes four inline midpoint copies, but the new helper re-creates getScheduledAmount's null/number/range dispatch alongside it, so two amount-resolution functions now coexist.

placement.why: The new helper sits in shared/schedules.ts next to the existing schedule amount logic and server callers import it from there, which matches the layering.

scope.why: Only the amount-resolution sites and a focused test are touched.

maintainability.why: Two near-identical exported helpers with different range rules (getScheduledAmount midpoint in the UI and schedule-template's own midpoint vs getExpectedScheduleAmount furthest-from-zero on the server) will confuse maintainers and let the displayed and posted amounts diverge.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Server sites (forecast-schedules normalizeSchedule, app.ts updateActions/postTransactionForSchedule, computeSchedulePreviewTransactions) are routed to a new getExpectedScheduleAmount instead of the existing getScheduledAmount helper.

disguised_duplication.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount in shared/schedules.ts is a renamed copy of getScheduledAmount's dispatch (null -> 0, number -> itself, range -> resolved value) with only the range arithmetic changed.

one_place.where: The new rule lives in getExpectedScheduleAmount, but getScheduledAmount (used by SchedulesTable, Balance, mobile schedule list/page) and server/budget/schedule-template.ts still compute the midpoint.
